summary: Modern databases and data platforms are increasingly embedding AI/ML capabilities directly into the engine, including native vector search, in-database model inference, and LLM integration, reducing the need for separate vector stores or model servers. By 2026, analysts project that 30% of enterprises will rely on vector-based retrieval for GenAI (up from ~2% in 2023) and 75% of enterprise AI applications will depend on vector search, though the value is shifting from standalone vector databases toward integrated platforms and the data preparation layer. Platforms like Snowflake, Databricks, MongoDB Atlas, and major cloud data warehouses now offer built-in vectorization, retrieval, and LLM functions as first-class features.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI (LLM functions, Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst)
databases.description: Cortex AI provides serverless access to LLMs and ML functions directly in SQL, including COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, TRANSLATE, SENTIMENT, EMBED_TEXT, and Cortex Search for RAG. Snowflake Postgres further unifies transactional Postgres data with analytics and AI on a single governed platform via the Horizon Catalog.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake supports a VECTOR data type with VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY/L2/INNER_PRODUCT functions and the managed Cortex Search service for semantic/hybrid retrieval, all built into the platform.
databases.llm_integration: Native hosted LLMs (Anthropic Claude, Mistral, Meta Llama, Snowflake Arctic, OpenAI via partnerships) accessible through Cortex SQL/Python functions and Cortex Agents.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based pricing in Snowflake credits; Cortex AI functions billed per token/credit usage on top of standard compute/storage. No separate license required.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML (in-SQL model training) + Vertex AI integration + ML.GENERATE_TEXT / ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets analysts create and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time series, boosting) using standard SQL without moving data. It integrates with Vertex AI for Gemini-based generative functions, embeddings, and remote model inference.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery supports VECTOR_SEARCH() with vector indexes (IVF/TreeAH) and the ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING function for in-warehouse embedding and semantic search.
databases.llm_integration: Native integration with Vertex AI Gemini models via remote models; ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING functions callable from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Pay-as-you-go: on-demand bytes-processed or capacity-based (slots) pricing, plus storage. Generative/remote model calls incur Vertex AI inference charges.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector extension for vector storage/search and pgai for in-database embeddings and LLM calls
databases.description: PostgreSQL gains AI capabilities through open-source extensions: pgvector adds a vector column type and similarity operators, while pgai (from Timescale) enables generating embeddings and calling LLMs (OpenAI, Ollama, etc.) from SQL. This keeps relational data, vectors, and AI workflows together in one mature engine with full ORM/driver support.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to core PostgreSQL. Vector search is provided by the pgvector extension (supporting HNSW and IVFFlat indexes); it must be installed/enabled. Core Postgres has no built-in vector type.
databases.llm_integration: Via extensions such as pgai (embedding generation and LLM completion from SQL) and pgvectorscale; not part of the core database.
databases.pricing_notes: Open-source and free; costs depend on hosting (self-managed or managed provider). External LLM/embedding API calls are billed separately by the model provider.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning (SQL-based integration with Amazon SageMaker, Bedrock, and Comprehend)
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you invoke ML models directly from SQL queries, passing row data to Amazon SageMaker (custom models), Amazon Bedrock (generative AI/LLMs), and Amazon Comprehend (sentiment/NLP) without building custom integration code. Results are returned as standard query columns.
databases.vector_search_notes: Aurora ML itself does not provide vector search. Vector search on Aurora PostgreSQL is available only via the pgvector extension, which must be enabled separately — it is not a native Aurora ML capability.
databases.llm_integration: SQL functions to call Amazon Bedrock foundation models (e.g., for text generation and embeddings) and Comprehend; LLM inference is delegated to AWS AI services.
databases.pricing_notes: Standard Aurora instance/storage/I/O pricing; no extra charge for the ML SQL integration, but underlying SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend invocations are billed by those services.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML (in-warehouse model creation via CREATE MODEL with Amazon SageMaker and Bedrock)
databases.description: Redshift ML enables data analysts and scientists to create, train, and deploy ML models using SQL CREATE MODEL statements, automatically leveraging Amazon SageMaker Autopilot behind the scenes. It supports prediction functions in SQL and integration with Bedrock for generative AI.
databases.vector_search_notes: Redshift ML does not provide native vector search. Redshift has introduced preview/limited vector capabilities, but as a service Redshift ML focuses on model training/inference, not vector similarity search.
databases.llm_integration: Integration with Amazon Bedrock foundation models for generative AI from SQL; training delegated to SageMaker.
databases.pricing_notes: Standard Redshift compute/storage pricing; model training uses SageMaker resources billed separately, while in-Redshift inference uses existing cluster compute.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI (model training, serving, agents) + Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks provides end-to-end AI via Mosaic AI for building, fine-tuning, and serving models and GenAI agents, plus Databricks Vector Search for RAG. It integrates with Unity Catalog for governance and offers Foundation Model APIs for LLM access.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a built-in managed vector database that automatically syncs and indexes embeddings from Delta tables for similarity and hybrid search.
databases.llm_integration: Native Foundation Model APIs and Model Serving for hosted and external LLMs (Llama, DBRX, Claude, OpenAI); Mosaic AI Agent Framework for building RAG/agent applications.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs) plus cloud infrastructure; Vector Search and Model Serving billed per compute/usage.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search (native vector indexing and semantic/hybrid search)
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search stores vector embeddings alongside operational document data and performs approximate nearest-neighbor search using the $vectorSearch aggregation stage. It enables RAG and semantic search directly on live application data without a separate vector store.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Atlas Vector Search is a built-in feature using HNSW-based indexes and the $vectorSearch operator, supporting pre-filtering and hybrid (vector + full-text) search within MongoDB.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with external LLM/embedding providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Hugging Face, Bedrock, Vertex AI) via frameworks like LangChain and LlamaIndex; no fully in-database hosted LLM.
databases.pricing_notes: Part of MongoDB Atlas managed service; priced via cluster tier/compute and dedicated Search Nodes for vector workloads.
